why: Count the shapes in each figure. Options 1, 2, 4 and 5 each have three shapes drawn one inside another (for example circle, square, triangle). Option 3 has only two shapes: a rectangle inside a parallelogram. The outer shapes change in every figure, so they are not the rule.
trick: When the shapes look random, count how many shapes are nested inside each figure.
